svg.text: The piece funnels from the lure of believing machines are conscious, into four independent arguments that knock
out the assumption behind that belief, then opens back out into what we should do about real versus merely seeming
conscious AI, looping back at the end to the embodied, biological view of mind it opened by setting against…

g.text: The Mythology Of Conscious AI — overview
A funnel (why we're tempted) narrows into a converge (four arguments against machine consciousness), then opens into
practical stakes, looping back to the essay's opening worry about mistaking ourselves for our machines.

g.text: Why we're tempted to see consciousness
A hub-and-satellite scene: one core confusion (intelligence mistaken for consciousness) is reinforced by three
overlapping biases, which together explain the illusion without proving anything about real machine experience.

g.text: So: dig deeper into computation itself
A converge: four independent lines of reasoning, each able to stand alone, meet at the same shaky conclusion about
whether computation alone can produce consciousness.
